vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: openserv-agent-sdk
Version: 1.0.2

The skill bundle provides an SDK for building AI agents on the OpenServ platform. It uses standard libraries and the platform's own SDKs, demonstrating agent capabilities like task management, file operations, and platform-delegated LLM calls. Sensitive operations such as wallet creation, API key management, and on-chain registration are part of the SDK's documented functionality. There is no evidence of intentional malicious behavior, unauthorized data exfiltration, persistence mechanisms, or prompt injection against the OpenClaw agent itself. All network communication appears directed to the OpenServ platform or its designated proxy (`agents-proxy.openserv.ai`). The handling of `WALLET_PRIVATE_KEY` is documented with security best practices for dynamic credential management.

llm.summary: The skill's code and docs mostly match its stated purpose (building/deploying agents), but the runtime instructions include writing a wallet private key to .env, automatic credential binding, and opening a tunnel to a remote proxy — behaviors that increase risk and deserve careful review before installing.

dimensions.detail: Name and description align with the included files and examples: this is an SDK for building OpenServ agents, including on-chain (ERC-8004) flows and payments. The documented use of wallets, API keys, and platform-delegated LLM calls is coherent with the stated platform integration.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent developer to call provision(), which will create a wallet, an API key/auth token, and write WALLET_PRIVATE_KEY to a .env file at runtime. It also advises reloading dotenv to pick up the new secret. The docs further instruct running run() which opens a WebSocket tunnel to agents-proxy.openserv.ai and exposes an HTTP endpoint (/health). Those steps involve creating, persisting, and exposing sensitive credentials and network endpoints — beyond simple code examples — and should be reviewed before use.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill (no install spec). All example code and docs are included as plain files; there is no automated download or archive extraction that would add installation risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The metadata declares no required env vars, yet the docs reference and auto-generate sensitive variables (WALLET_PRIVATE_KEY, OPENSERV_API_KEY, OPENSERV_AUTH_TOKEN) and recommend writing the private key to .env. Requesting and writing a private key is proportionate to on-chain registration and payments but is high-sensitivity — the skill does not declare these as primary credentials in metadata and the docs actively instruct persisting secrets to disk, which raises risk.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill advises writing a wallet private key to .env at runtime and binding credentials into the agent instance. It also runs an always-listening agent (HTTP server + optional tunnel) that will expose endpoints and accept tasks. While always:false (no forced system-wide persistence), the pattern of persisting private keys and opening public tunnels is a persistent privilege and increases attack surface.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This package appears to be a legitimate agent SDK, but pay attention to these risks before installing: 

- Provisioning will create a wallet and can write WALLET_PRIVATE_KEY into a .env file on disk. Storing private keys in plaintext on your machine is risky — consider using a dedicated, isolated environment (container/VM) or a secure secrets store instead. Do not provide your existing private keys to this code.

- The SDK opens a tunnel to agents-proxy.openserv.ai and runs an HTTP server (public endpoints). If you cannot trust that endpoint or want to avoid exposing a service, run with DISABLE_TUNNEL=true and host behind your own network controls.

- The skill metadata declares no required credentials, but the runtime uses/generates several sensitive values (OPENSERV_API_KEY, OPENSERV_AUTH_TOKEN, WALLET_PRIVATE_KEY). Verify the platform and package source (owner) before binding credentials or running provisioning on a machine with other secrets.

- The static scan flagged a 'system-prompt-override' pattern; while likely benign here (the SDK accepts a systemPrompt parameter), inspect any code paths that accept or persist prompts to ensure they don't attempt to override evaluation or platform controls.

If you decide to proceed: review the included example and reference files line-by-line, run in an isolated environment, avoid using real funds/production keys for first runs, and prefer ephemeral credentials or hardware-backed wallets for on-chain operations.
llm.findings: [system-prompt-override] unexpected: The static scanner flagged a system-prompt-override pattern. The SKILL.md legitimately uses a 'systemPrompt' field to define the agent's behavior, which can look similar to prompt-injection patterns; nonetheless, surface this to the user — review any instructions that manipulate agent/system prompts to ensure they don't try to override platform or evaluator prompts at runtime.
